title: Constructibility of all reductions from the first one

proof.text: Put $t=\pi_E$, $B=\mathcal O_{E,X}$, $\Lambda_j=\mathcal O_E/t^j$ and $R_j=(\Lambda_j)_X$. The extension absolute value, DVR and finite-quotient lemmas give that every $\Lambda_j$ is finite. Apply the finite-coefficient model comparison to identify both constructibility conventions, retaining the same vanishing intervals.

source.place: Second paragraph: finite quotient rings and constructibility conventions.

proof.text: The first assertion of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] gives injectivity of $t$ on $B$ and $R_j=B/t^jB$. Apply [lem-pe-successive-quotient-linear-triangle] for $n>1$: in $D(R_n)$ the outer terms of its triangle are the scalar restrictions of $K_{n-1}$ and $K_1$, and the middle term is $K_n$.

source.place: Second paragraph: coefficient exact sequence and derived tensor triangle.

proof.text: Assume (1), choosing $r\le s$ with $H^q(K_1)=0$ outside $[r,s]$. Induct on $n\ge1$ with simultaneous claims: $K_n$ is bounded constructible and has this same bound. The base is (1). At $n>1$, [lem-pe-finite-scalar-restriction-constructible] puts both outer triangle terms in the bounded constructible category over the finite ring $\Lambda_n$, without changing bounds. The distinguished-triangle clause of [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] gives constructibility of $K_n$. The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] contains $H^q(\operatorname{Res}K_{n-1})\to H^q(K_n)\to H^q(\operatorname{Res}K_1)$. Outside $[r,s]$ both outer terms vanish, so exactness forces the middle term to vanish. This completes the induction and proves (2).

source.place: Second paragraph: induction, constructible extension closure and uniform interval.

proof.text: For the final interpretation apply [lem-pe-integral-completion-presentation] to the already complete $K$: its completed-coefficient reduction tower is the same tower, and it satisfies the completeness condition used by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Finite-torsion constructibility [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] imposes literally the clauses of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] for $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ (finite partition into locally closed constructible strata, locally constant restrictions, finite module stalks), so by [lem-pe-finite-coefficient-model-comparison] it is precisely the constructibility used above. By [def-weil-cohomological-support], support in $[r,s]$ means vanishing outside it. Thus the remaining defining conditions are exactly (2), hence equivalent to (1). This final interpretation uses the global range $\ell\ne p$ of that definition; the equivalence (1)--(2) itself does not require it. No Tor-amplitude condition is added.

source.place: Statement final sentence: interpret the all-reductions criterion.

proof_origin.place: Both paragraphs: the coefficient exact-sequence induction, expanded using existing general tools.
